processing: Orthodox Darjeeling processing as is usual for the district, with lighter oxidation in spring. The garden is listed as organic.
harvest_season: As usual in Darjeeling, first flush in spring and second flush in early summer, then monsoon and autumn pickings.
appearance_dry: Typical of Darjeeling, twisted olive-and-brown leaf with some pale tips.
appearance_liquor: Pale gold to amber, depending on the flush.
appearance_wet: Soft green-and-copper leaf in spring, browner later.
taste_profile: Little is recorded about this garden's own cup. As with other Darjeelings, expect a floral, brisk spring tea and a fruitier summer one.

brewing.notes: Western-style. Use about 85°C for a spring lot.

vintage_note: Usual for Darjeeling: sold by year and flush, with lot numbers and grades on single-estate tea. Spring lots are best within about a year. Look for the organic mark and a stated flush.
description:
Sivitar is a garden in the Kurseong area of Darjeeling, a neighbour of two much better-known names, Goomtee and Jungpana. It belongs to Darjeeling Organic Tea Estates and appears on lists of organic gardens.

Specifics of its processing are scarce, so expect the usual orthodox Darjeeling method, with light oxidation in spring and fuller oxidation in summer.

Brew it as you would other Darjeelings. Tasting a Sivitar against a Goomtee or Jungpana of the same flush is a good way to see how much a famous name is really worth.

Few lots appear under this name, so buy on the year and flush stated rather than on reputation.
history:
The garden's name is said to come from a hill with a river at its foot, thought to recall a Shiva lingam, according to the group that runs it. A date of 1870 is sometimes linked with it, but its founding year is not firmly documented.

It is now part of Darjeeling Organic Tea Estates, whose gardens have been moving to organic farming.
